info.title: RiskOS API
info.description:
RiskOS public HTTP contract. This file is the single source of truth: Go server stubs and the
TypeScript client are generated from it (`make generate`), and CI fails if generated code drifts.

**Authentication.** Every `/api/v1` operation requires an API key sent as
`Authorization: Bearer rsk_test_…` (test environment) or `rsk_live_…` (production). The key
determines the tenant and environment; no request field can change them. A key can only act
within its own environment and only with the scopes it holds.

**Errors** use one contract: `{"error":{"code","message","request_id"}}`.

**Idempotency.** `POST /api/v1/events` is idempotent on the event's `event_id` within the
key's environment. Retrying with the same payload returns the original response with the
header `Idempotent-Replay: true`; the same `event_id` with a different payload is rejected with
`409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`.

**Rate limits.** Requests are limited per API key and per tenant. Excess requests get
`429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After` (seconds).

**Pagination.** List operations return `data` and `next_cursor`. Pass `next_cursor` back as
`cursor` to get the next page; `next_cursor` is null on the last page. Results are newest first.

tags.description:
The jurisdiction rule pack a workspace is on (ADR-0006): regulatory controls, risk-scoring
rules and governance presets, each with its legal source, effective date, verification status
and the library's plain-English wording.

get.description: Returns 200 while the process is running and able to serve HTTP. Performs no dependency checks.

Returns 200 when every required dependency (PostgreSQL, Redis) answered within its check
timeout, and 503 otherwise, including while the server is draining during shutdown.
Per-dependency status is reported without internal error details.

503.description: Not ready; at least one dependency is unavailable or the server is draining.

get.description: Returns the tenant, environment and scopes the presented API key resolves to. Requires no scope.

get.summary: List API keys of the caller's environment
get.description: Requires scope `api_keys:read`. Secrets are never returned.

post.summary: Create an API key in the caller's environment
post.description:
Requires scope `api_keys:write`. The new key can only receive scopes the caller holds.
The secret is returned **once**, in this response; store it immediately.

201.description: Created. Contains the only copy of the secret.

post.summary: Rotate an API key
post.description:
Requires scope `api_keys:write` and every scope of the rotated key. Creates a replacement
with the same name and scopes and returns its secret once. The old key keeps working for
the overlap window, then expires. A revoked or already-rotated key cannot be rotated.

201.description: The replacement key. Contains the only copy of its secret.

post.summary: Revoke an API key
post.description:
Requires scope `api_keys:write`. Takes effect within seconds on every instance. Revoking an
already revoked key returns it unchanged.

get.description:
Requires scope `audit_logs:read`. Returns tenant-level entries and entries of the caller's
environment. Each entry carries its position in the tenant's hash chain.

post.summary: Ingest an event and get its risk decision
post.description:
Requires scope `events:write`. Validates, normalizes and stores the event, evaluates it
and returns the decision in the same response. Idempotent on `event_id` (see above).
Timestamps must be at most 5 minutes in the future and 24 hours in the past.
Card numbers, CVVs, PINs and passwords must never be sent; payloads containing
card-number-like values are rejected.

200.description: The risk decision. Replays carry `Idempotent-Replay: true`.

get.summary: List events of the caller's environment
get.description:
Requires scope `events:read`. Newest first. Every filter is optional. `after` returns
only events newer than the given event (the live monitor polls with it).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only events newer than this event ID.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Only events of this user (actor.user_id).

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: Only events of this account (actor.account_id).

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Only events from this device (actor.device_id).

get.summary: A user's, account's or device's profile
get.description:
Requires scope `events:read`. Built from the entity's most recent 5,000 events: activity,
scores, decisions, and the users, accounts, devices, countries and IP addresses seen with
it. 404 when the environment has no events for it.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The identifier you send as actor.user_id, account_id or device_id.

get.summary: Decisions, scores and signals over time
get.description:
Requires scope `events:read`. Events per bucket (hourly for 24h and 7d, daily for 30d),
the highest-risk users and the signals that fired most, over the window.

get.summary: Get an event with its payloads and evaluation
get.description: Requires scope `events:read`.

post.summary: Evaluate an event without ingesting it (dry run)
post.description:
Requires scope `risk:evaluate`. Runs the same validation and evaluation as ingestion but
stores no event; the evaluation is recorded as a dry run and never raises alerts or
webhooks. Not idempotent: every call is evaluated.

get.summary: Built-in signals and the fields rules can use
get.description: Requires scope `rules:read`. Includes each signal's default and effective weight for the caller's environment.

get.summary: The environment's risk bands, thresholds and default decisions
get.description:
Readable with any of `events:read`, `alerts:read`, `cases:read`, `rules:read`,
`risk:evaluate` or `risk:configure`: everyone who sees scores can see how they are banded.
Requires scope `risk:configure`. Returns product defaults until settings are saved.

put.description:
Requires scope `risk:configure`. Audited. Built-in signal weights may be tuned between 0
and 50; changes apply within seconds.

get.summary: List rules with their current versions
get.description: Requires scope `rules:read`.

post.summary: Create a rule
post.description:
Requires scope `rules:write`. Audited. Start new rules in `shadow` mode: they are evaluated
on live traffic and recorded, but do not change decisions until switched to `active`.
Returns 409 when the code is taken or the environment already has 200 rules (disabled
rules count; rules are disabled, never deleted).
In a production environment the change is proposed instead (202) and applies only when
another person approves it.

201.description: The created rule (version 1). Test environments apply changes at once.

202.description:
Production environments: the change was proposed and awaits approval by another person
(two-person rule). Nothing has changed yet; approve it with
`POST /api/v1/rule-changes/{change_id}/approve`.

get.summary: How often each of the workspace's rules matched
get.description:
Requires `rules:read`. For every rule of the environment, how many evaluations it matched
(active and monitoring alike) over the last `days` days, the last match and a count per UTC
day, beside the number of evaluations in the period. Dry runs are not counted.

post.summary: Try a condition on recent events
post.description:
Requires `rules:read`. Runs a condition, saved or not, against the facts of the
environment's most recent evaluations (at most 5,000, within `days` days) and says how
many it would have matched, with up to 25 of them, newest first. Nothing is stored and no
score changes. The facts are those recorded at the time; behaviour that has changed since
is not recomputed.

200.description: What the condition would have matched.

get.description: Requires scope `rules:read`.

patch.summary: Change a rule (creates a new version)
patch.description:
Requires scope `rules:write`. Audited. Only the given fields change. Every change creates a
new version; earlier versions are kept and can be restored. A change that alters nothing
creates no version.
In a production environment the change is proposed instead (202) and applies only when
another person approves it.

200.description: The rule with its (possibly new) current version.

202.description:
Production environments: the change was proposed and awaits approval by another person
(two-person rule). Nothing has changed yet; approve it with
`POST /api/v1/rule-changes/{change_id}/approve`.

get.description: Requires scope `rules:read`. Newest first.

post.summary: Restore an earlier version (one-step rollback)
post.description:
Requires scope `rules:write`. Audited. Adds a new version with the content of the given
version; history is never rewritten.
In a production environment the change is proposed instead (202) and applies only when
another person approves it.

200.description: The rule with the restored content as its new current version.

202.description:
Production environments: the change was proposed and awaits approval by another person
(two-person rule). Nothing has changed yet; approve it with
`POST /api/v1/rule-changes/{change_id}/approve`.

post.summary: Test a rule against an event
post.description:
Requires scope `rules:read`. Evaluates the rule's current condition, or a draft
`condition`, against the event using the environment's live features without changing
them. Nothing is stored. Returns whether it matched and the values of the fields the
condition uses.

get.description:
Requires `rules:read` or `risk:configure`. Newest first, at most 1,000. Events whose user,
account, device, IP address, beneficiary or country is listed (and not expired) are
blocked, whatever their score.

post.summary: Add an identifier to the deny list
post.description:
Requires `risk:configure`. Audited. Takes effect within seconds. IP addresses are stored
in canonical form and countries upper-case; other identifiers must match exactly what you
send in events. 409 when the identifier is already listed or the environment has 10,000
entries.

delete.summary: Remove an identifier from the deny list
delete.description: Requires `risk:configure`. Audited. Takes effect within seconds.

get.description: Requires scope `rules:read`. Newest first, at most 200.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only changes in this state (default pending).

get.description: Requires scope `rules:read`.

post.summary: Approve a proposed rule change (applies it)
post.description:
Requires the `rules:approve` permission, which only people hold (never API keys), and a
recent second factor in the console. The approver must not be the person who proposed
the change. Applies the change as the rule's next version; returns 409 if the rule has
changed since the proposal (propose again) or the change is already decided. Audited.

200.description: The approved change, with the version it created.

post.summary: Reject or withdraw a proposed rule change
post.description:
Requires `rules:approve`, or `rules:write` for the person or key that proposed the change
(withdrawing it). Nothing changes on the rule. Audited.

get.description: Requires scope `alerts:read`.

get.summary: Get an alert with its evaluations and timeline
get.description: Requires scope `alerts:read`. Returns the newest 100 evaluations the alert groups.

patch.description:
Requires scope `alerts:write`. Audited. Allowed status changes: `open` and `investigating`
to any of `open`, `investigating`, `false_positive`, `resolved`. `false_positive` and
`resolved` are final. Alerts are escalated by creating a case with them
(`POST /api/v1/cases`); an escalated alert is closed by resolving its case. An empty
`assignee` unassigns. A change that alters nothing is a no-op.

get.description: Requires scope `cases:read`.

post.summary: Open a case, optionally escalating alerts into it
post.description:
Requires scope `cases:write`, and `alerts:write` when `alert_ids` are given. Audited. Every
listed alert must be `open` or `investigating`; they become `escalated`. Without a
`priority`, the case takes the highest severity of its alerts (`medium` without alerts).

get.summary: Get a case with its alerts, notes and timeline
get.description: Requires scope `cases:read`.

patch.description:
Requires scope `cases:write`. Audited. Resolving (`status: resolved`) requires a
`resolution` and closes the case's alerts: `false_positive` when the resolution is
`false_positive`, otherwise `resolved`. A resolved case is final; notes can still be added.
An empty `assignee` unassigns.

post.summary: Add a note to a case
post.description:
Requires scope `cases:write`. Notes are append-only: they cannot be edited or deleted. Do
not put card numbers, passwords or other secrets in notes.

get.description: Requires scope `webhooks:read`.

post.summary: Register a webhook endpoint
post.description:
Requires scope `webhooks:write`. Audited. The response contains the endpoint's signing secret,
shown only this once. URLs must use https and must not point to localhost or private,
loopback, link-local or reserved addresses (also checked after DNS resolution on every
delivery). At most 20 endpoints per environment (409 beyond).

get.description: Requires scope `webhooks:read`. Never returns the secret.

patch.summary: Change or enable/disable a webhook endpoint
patch.description:
Requires scope `webhooks:write`. Audited. Setting `status: active` re-enables an endpoint
disabled after failing, and clears its failure state.

post.summary: Rotate a webhook endpoint's signing secret
post.description:
Requires scope `webhooks:write`. Audited. Returns the new secret, shown only this once.
Until the overlap ends, deliveries carry signatures from both the new and the previous
secret, so receivers can switch without dropping events.

200.description: The endpoint and its new secret.

post.summary: Send a test event to an endpoint
post.description: Requires scope `webhooks:write`. Queues a `webhook.test` event for this endpoint only.

get.summary: List an endpoint's deliveries, newest first
get.description: Requires scope `webhooks:read`.

get.summary: Get a delivery with its payload and every attempt
get.description: Requires scope `webhooks:read`.

post.summary: Retry a failed delivery
post.description:
Requires scope `webhooks:write`. Audited. Starts a new delivery cycle for a `failed` delivery
to an active endpoint. The event keeps its ID.

post.summary: Sign in to the console with email and password
post.description:
Starts a console session. The response says which second factor is needed next
(`mfa_required`) or that the user must enroll one (`enrollment_required`); the cookie is set
either way. Wrong email, wrong password and disabled accounts get the same 401. Attempts are
throttled per email and per IP (429). Not for API keys.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure outside local development).

get.description:
Returns the signed-in user, tenant, role, permissions, second factors, the session's state
and the CSRF token the console must send in `X-CSRF-Token` on every unsafe request.

post.summary: Sign out
post.description: Ends the session and clears the cookie.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure outside local development).

post.summary: Verify an authenticator-app code
post.description:
Completes sign-in (`mfa_required`) or re-authenticates an active session for high-impact
actions. Each code works once. Throttled per user.

post.summary: Use a recovery code
post.description: Like `verifyTotp` with one of the single-use recovery codes.

200.description: The session's state and the codes left.

post.summary: Start authenticator-app enrollment
post.description:
For a new user (`enrollment_required`), or an active session re-authenticated within the
last 10 minutes. Returns the secret and an `otpauth://` URI for a QR code.

post.summary: Confirm authenticator-app enrollment
post.description:
Confirms enrollment with a first code. Returns recovery codes, shown once, if the user had
none. A new user's session becomes active.

200.description: The session's state (with recovery codes when issued).

post.summary: Start adding a passkey
post.description: Returns WebAuthn `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions` for `navigator.credentials.create`. Same conditions as `enrollTotp`.

post.summary: Finish adding a passkey
post.description: Verifies the authenticator's response and stores the passkey. Returns recovery codes, shown once, if the user had none.

post.summary: Start a passkey verification
post.description: Returns WebAuthn `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions` for `navigator.credentials.get`, to complete sign-in or re-authenticate.

post.summary: Finish a passkey verification
post.description: Verifies the assertion. Completes sign-in or re-authenticates.

delete.description: Requires re-authentication within the last 10 minutes. At least one second factor must remain.

post.summary: Replace your recovery codes
post.description: Requires re-authentication within the last 10 minutes. The new codes are shown once; the old ones stop working.

post.summary: Accept an invite
post.description:
Creates the invited user with a name and password and starts a session that must enroll a
second factor next. Invites are single-use and expire after 72 hours.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure outside local development).

get.description: Requires `team:read`.

patch.summary: Change a user's role or status
patch.description:
Requires `team:write` and, from the console, re-authentication within the last 10 minutes.
Audited. You cannot change yourself; the tenant always keeps an active administrator. Any
change ends the user's sessions.

get.description: Requires `team:read`.

post.summary: Invite a person
post.description:
Requires `team:write` and, from the console, re-authentication within the last 10 minutes.
Audited. Returns a single-use link, valid for 72 hours and shown once. When RiskOS has email
configured, the link is also emailed to the person (`email_queued`).

post.summary: Revoke a pending invite
post.description: Requires `team:write`. Audited.

post.summary: Start signing in with the tenant's identity provider
post.description:
For a person whose tenant uses single sign-on (OpenID Connect). Returns the provider's
authorization URL to send the browser to, and sets a short-lived cookie binding the request to
this browser. Unknown emails, disabled accounts and tenants without SSO all get 404
`SSO_NOT_CONFIGURED`. Throttled per email and per IP (429). SSO signs in existing accounts only,
and RiskOS still asks for its own second factor afterwards.

Set-Cookie.description: The request's browser binding (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, ten minutes).

post.summary: Finish signing in with the tenant's identity provider
post.description:
Called by the console's callback page with the provider's `code` and `state`. The request must
have been started in this browser within ten minutes, and the provider's ID token must verify.
The first SSO sign-in also needs the provider to confirm the account's email
(`email_verified`); it binds the provider's subject to the account, and later sign-ins must
present the same subject. Starts a console session exactly like `login`: the response says
which second factor is needed next. Failures get 401 `SSO_FAILED`.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure outside local development).

get.summary: Which ways to sign up are available
get.description:
`email` is false when sign-up is switched off or RiskOS cannot send email; `google` is true
when Google sign-in is configured. The console shows only what is available.

200.description: The available ways to sign up.

post.summary: Start creating a workspace with email and password
post.description:
Records the sign-up and emails a 6-digit code to prove the address; nothing is created until
the code is verified. The response is the same whether or not the email already has an
account (that person gets an email saying so instead of a code). Passwords follow the console
rules (12 to 128 characters, not the email, not in known breaches). Sets a cookie, valid for an
hour, that ties the sign-up to this browser. Throttled per email and per IP (429).

202.description: A code is on its way.

Set-Cookie.description: The sign-up's browser binding (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, one hour).

post.summary: Send a new code
post.description:
Sends a new code (the previous one stops working), at most once a minute and five times per
sign-up (429 with Retry-After).

200.description: A new code is on its way.

post.summary: Verify the emailed code and create the workspace
post.description:
With the right code, creates the workspace (a tenant with test and production environments,
production locked until onboarding is approved) and its first administrator, and starts a
session that must enroll a second factor next. A wrong code gets 400 `CODE_INVALID`; five
wrong codes end the sign-up (start again).

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure outside local development).

post.summary: Name the workspace and create it (Google sign-ups)
post.description:
For a sign-up whose email Google verified: creates the workspace with this business name and
its first administrator, and starts a session that must enroll a second factor next.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure outside local development).

post.summary: Start signing in or up with Google
post.description:
Returns Google's authorization URL and sets a short-lived cookie binding the request to this
browser. 404 `GOOGLE_NOT_CONFIGURED` when Google sign-in is not set up.

Set-Cookie.description: The request's browser binding (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, ten minutes).

post.summary: Finish signing in or up with Google
post.description:
Called by the console's Google callback page with Google's `code` and `state`. Google must
confirm the email (`email_verified`). If the email has an account, its first Google sign-in
binds Google's subject (later ones must match) and a session starts that still needs RiskOS's
second factor (`outcome: signed_in`). Otherwise a sign-up starts with the verified email
(`outcome: needs_business`): name the workspace with `completeSignup`. Failures get 401
`GOOGLE_FAILED`.

200.description: Signed in, or a sign-up waiting for its business name.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie, or the sign-up's browser binding.

get.description:
Requires `team:read`. 404 for workspaces created by RiskOS operators (they have no onboarding).
`missing` lists the answers still needed before submitting.

put.description:
Requires `team:write`. Replaces the answers; allowed while the onboarding is a draft or was
rejected (saving a rejected one makes it a draft again). 409 once submitted or approved.

post.summary: Submit the onboarding for review
post.description:
Requires `team:write`. Every required answer must be present (400 lists what is missing).
RiskOS staff then review it; approval opens the production environment.

get.summary: The jurisdictions with a rule pack
get.description:
Requires `compliance:read`. The latest version of every loaded jurisdiction pack, with its
rule counts, and which one the workspace's profile uses.

get.summary: The countries RiskOS has a rule pack for
get.description:
Requires `compliance:read`. Every jurisdiction with its currency, time zone, regulators and
pack, and whether the workspace has activated it (ADR-0007).

Requires `compliance:read`. One activation per country and booking entity: the pack it is on,
the institution type, its status (draft, shadow, live or suspended) and whether it is the
fallback that judges events naming no booking entity (ADR-0007).

get.summary: Every pack rule running for the workspace
get.description:
Requires `compliance:read`. Every rule of every activated country that applies to the
activation and runs in this environment (live or shadow), with the events that trigger it and
the facts and references to send for it to be evaluated. A rule whose `unset_settings` is not
empty, or whose facts are not sent, is reported as not evaluated in decisions. Your own rules
are at `/api/v1/rules`.

parameters.name: jurisdiction
parameters.description: Only rules of this country.

200.description: The active rules, by country and ID.

get.description:
Requires `compliance:read`. The pack version on the workspace's compliance profile, or the most
recently loaded pack when no profile is set; with `jurisdiction`, another jurisdiction's
latest pack, to browse.

parameters.name: jurisdiction
parameters.description:
Browse another jurisdiction's pack (its latest version), read-only: no applicability and
the library's default modes. Without it, the workspace's own pack.

get.description:
Requires `compliance:read`. Every rule of the pack, ordered by ID, with its wording, source,
effective date, verification status, defaults and bounded parameters. The engineering logic
is only on a single rule, for callers with `compliance:engineering`.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Only rules in this group.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only rules of this kind.

parameters.name: regulator
parameters.description: Only rules involving this regulator (CBN, NFIU and so on).

parameters.name: verification
parameters.description: Only rules with this verification status.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Words to find in a rule's ID, name or description.

parameters.name: applicable
parameters.description: Only rules that do (true) or do not (false) apply to the workspace's licence type and capabilities. Needs a compliance profile.

parameters.name: jurisdiction
parameters.description:
Browse another jurisdiction's pack (its latest version), read-only: no applicability and
the library's default modes. Without it, the workspace's own pack.

get.description:
Requires `compliance:read`. `engineering_logic` (the library's section 7B) and `definition` (the
machine definition) are included only for callers with `compliance:engineering`.

parameters.name: jurisdiction
parameters.description:
The country whose pack the rule is in. Without it, the jurisdiction a country rule ID names
(GH-REG-01 is Ghana's), else the workspace's fallback pack.

get.summary: A rule's configuration in this environment
get.description: Requires `compliance:read`. Version 0 means the library's defaults.

put.summary: Set a rule's mode and settings in this environment
put.description:
Requires `compliance:configure` (people only) and, in the console, a recent second factor.
`settings` lists values that differ from the library's defaults; each must be within the
setting's bounds (for regulatory limits, the legal maximum). Omitted settings use the
default. Applied at once (200), except in production for a regulatory control when any
setting changes or the mode moves away from live: that is proposed (202) and applies when
another person with `rules:approve` approves it. Audited.

202.description: Proposed; applies when another person approves it.

get.summary: A rule's configuration versions in this environment
get.description: Requires `compliance:read`. Newest first; versions never change.

post.summary: Restore an earlier configuration as a new version
post.description:
Requires `compliance:configure` and, in the console, a recent second factor. The same
approval rule as a configuration change applies.

202.description: Proposed; applies when another person approves it.

post.summary: What a rule would have done over recent events
post.description:
Requires `compliance:read` and `events:read`. Replays this environment's ingested events of
the last `days` (default 7, at most 30; at most 20,000 events) through the rule with
`settings` (values that differ from the defaults; omitted: the current configuration) and
with its current configuration, whatever its mode, with time windows rebuilt in memory.
Nothing is stored and live state is untouched. Events evaluated before the rule pack ran
are not replayed.

200.description: The two configurations' results over the same events.

get.description:
Requires `compliance:read`. US dollars per one unit of each currency, used to compute
`txn.amount_usd` for rules on US dollar amounts (REG-10) when the event does not send it.

put.description:
Requires `compliance:write` (people only) and, in the console, a recent second factor.
Audited. Applies to every environment within 5 seconds.

usd_per_unit.description: US dollars per one unit of the currency (for NGN, about 0.00065).

get.description:
Requires `compliance:sensitive`, held only by compliance officers (GOV-09). Rules marked
compliance-only (such as INS-01, staff-linked accounts) add their points to the score
under the code `compliance_review` everywhere else: in decisions, events, alerts, webhooks
and analytics. This lists the evaluations where one fired, with the rule itself, newest
first, at most 200.

Requires `compliance:read`. What fired regulatory controls require (reports to the NFIU,
enhanced due diligence, freezing or closing an account), open ones first by deadline, at
most 500. Suspicious transaction reports are listed only for `compliance:sensitive`
(GOV-09). For callers who read alerts, `escalations` lists alerts still open past REG-14's
screening deadline (72 hours by default) and high or critical alerts nobody acted on
within GOV-11's response target (30 minutes by default). For callers who read cases,
`unreported_fraud` lists cases resolved as confirmed fraud without an industry fraud
report (GOV-12), at most 200.
Requires `compliance:read`, and `compliance:sensitive` for a suspicious transaction report.

patch.description:
Requires `compliance:write`, and `compliance:sensitive` for a suspicious transaction report.
Only a draft (open) report changes. Omitted fields are unchanged.

post.summary: Approve a report for filing
post.description:
Requires `compliance:sensitive`: only compliance officers approve reports (GOV-06), and in
the console a recent second factor. A suspicious transaction report is approved only when
goAML would accept it: a predicate offence, at least one indicator and an accepted
category (REG-19); otherwise 400 says what is missing. Audited.

post.summary: Record that a report was filed
post.description:
Requires `compliance:sensitive`. Records that a person filed the approved report with the
regulator, with the reference its portal gave. RiskOS never submits reports. Audited.

post.summary: Mark a task done or dismiss it
post.description:
Requires `compliance:write`, and `compliance:sensitive` for a suspicious transaction report.
Reports are closed by filing them; dismissing any task needs a note. Audited.

get.summary: An approved report, for filing by hand
get.description:
Requires `compliance:write`, and `compliance:sensitive` for a suspicious transaction report.
Returns the approved report for a person to enter in the regulator's portal. Audited.

post.summary: Prepare an industry fraud report for a confirmed-fraud case
post.description:
Requires `compliance:write`. Opens a draft industry fraud report (GOV-12) for a case
resolved as confirmed fraud, prefilled from the case. A compliance officer approves it and
a person files it with the industry channel (NIBSS) and records the reference: RiskOS
never submits it. One report per case unless it was dismissed (409). No deadline is
set: the source does not state one. Audited.

post.summary: Confirm suspicion on a case
post.description:
Requires `compliance:sensitive` (compliance officers) and, in the console, a recent second
factor. Opens a suspicious transaction report for the case, due within REG-14's `str_due`
(24 hours by default) from now. Nothing about it is visible outside compliance roles
(GOV-09). Audited.

note.description: The first lines of the report's narrative.

get.description: Requires `compliance:read`. Newest first, at most 200.

post.summary: Approve a pending change
post.description:
Requires `rules:approve` (people only) and, in the console, a recent second factor. Nobody
can approve their own change. Applies the change as the rule's next version, credited to
its proposer, only if the rule has not changed since (409 otherwise). Audited.

post.summary: Reject or withdraw a pending change
post.description: Requires `rules:approve`, or being the change's proposer (withdrawing it). Audited.

get.description: Requires `compliance:read`. The reporting and response deadlines the pack's workflows time.

parameters.description: The country whose pack to read; without it, the workspace's fallback pack.

get.summary: Legal clocks and thresholds side by side
get.description:
Requires `compliance:read`. The library's comparison of Nigeria, Ghana and Rwanda, with the
working default for a multi-country workspace, verbatim (ADR-0007). "Not found" means no
readable source gave a number.

Requires `compliance:read`. Every rule of a country's pack (or of every pack) in plain English,
with its provenance, the settings in use in this environment, caveats and sources, as CSV or
PDF, built on the server. Audited.

parameters.description: The country; without it, every country with a pack.

parameters.description: The country whose pack to read; without it, the workspace's fallback pack.

put.description:
Requires `compliance:write` (people only). Sets the jurisdiction, licence type and capabilities
that decide which rules apply. Saving adopts the jurisdiction's latest pack version
(`latest_version` on the pack); rule configuration carries over. Audited.

get.description:
Requires `team:read`. `connection` is null when SSO is not set up. The client secret is never
returned.

200.description: The redirect URI to register at the provider, and the connection.

put.summary: Set up or change single sign-on
put.description:
Requires `team:write` and, from the console, re-authentication within the last 10 minutes.
Audited (without the secret). RiskOS reads the issuer's OpenID Connect discovery document
first and refuses an issuer it cannot read (400). `client_secret` is required the first time;
leave it out to keep the stored one. Changing the issuer forgets the provider subjects bound
to accounts.

delete.description:
Requires `team:write` and, from the console, re-authentication. Audited. People sign in with
their password again.

XRequestID.description:
Correlation ID for this request. Echoes a caller-supplied `X-Request-ID` when it is 1-64
characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`; otherwise a server-generated `req_…` ID.

DefaultError.description: Error in the standard RiskOS error contract (spec §7).

InvalidRequest.description: `INVALID_REQUEST`: the request is malformed or fails validation.

Unauthenticated.description: `UNAUTHENTICATED`: the API key is missing, malformed, unknown, revoked or expired. The response never says which.

Forbidden.description: `FORBIDDEN`: the key lacks a required scope. `TENANT_SUSPENDED`: the tenant is not active.

NotFound.description: `NOT_FOUND`: the resource does not exist in the caller's environment. Resources of other tenants or environments are indistinguishable from nonexistent ones.

Conflict.description: `CONFLICT`: the resource is not in a state that allows the operation. `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`: the event_id was already used with a different payload.

Unprocessable.description: `STALE_EVENT`: occurred_at is outside the accepted window. `INVALID_EVENT`: the event is well-formed but semantically invalid. `SENSITIVE_DATA`: the payload contains data that must never be sent (e.g. a card number).

RateLimited.description: `RATE_LIMITED`: too many requests for this API key or tenant.

email.description: Sign-up with email, business name and password is available.

google.description: Signing in and up with Google is available.

resend_after_seconds.description: How long until another code can be requested.

expires_at.description: When the sign-up lapses (start again after).

OnboardingAnswers.description:
Know-your-business answers. Every field is optional while drafting; `submitOnboarding`
requires the ones listed in `Onboarding.missing`.

regulated.description: Licensed or registered with a financial regulator.

screening_provider.description: Sanctions and PEP screening provider, if any.

truncated.description: The event limit cut the period short; the replay covers its oldest events.

missing.description: What made the rule not evaluated, most frequent first.

fired_samples.description: Events the rule fired on (at most 20, oldest first).

ComplianceTaskStatus.description: Reports go open (a draft), approved, filed; other tasks open, done. Any may be dismissed.

kind.description: report.STR, report.CTR, report.FTR, report.PEP_monthly, report.sanctions, report.industry_fraud, case.open, edd, source_of_funds, source_of_wealth, senior_approval, freeze_account or close_account.

sensitive.description: A suspicious transaction report, seen only by compliance officers.

account_ref.description: The account it concerns (REG-16 closes accounts without a BVN).

report.description: The report's fields (category, predicate offence, indicators, narrative, amount...).

ScreeningEscalation.description: An alert still open past a deadline of the pack.

rule.description: REG-14 (screening deadline) or GOV-11 (fraud response target).

UnreportedFraudCase.description: A case resolved as confirmed fraud without an industry fraud report (GOV-12).

PackRuleMode.description: live (it acts), shadow (it is evaluated and recorded only) or off.

PackRuleSettings.description: Settings that differ from the library's defaults, by name, in the setting's unit.

reason.description: Why, for the audit log and the approver.

version.description: 0 while the rule runs with the library's defaults.

pending.description: The change awaiting a second person, if any.

ComplianceRuleKind.description: control (a regulatory hard control), signal (a risk-scoring rule) or governance (a process requirement).

ComplianceVerification.description: How far the rule's legal facts are confirmed. Anything but confirmed comes with a caveat.

rules.description: How many rules the group has.

latest_version.description: The newest loaded version for the jurisdiction. When it differs from `version`, saving the compliance profile adopts it.

checksum.description: SHA-256 of the pack's files. A loaded version never changes.

currency.description: Amounts in the pack's settings are in minor units of this currency (or US dollars).

timezone.description: The time zone the pack's windows and hours of the day are kept in.

penalties.description: The library's penalty exposure register, for display. Estimates marked as inference are not law.

estimate.description: The amount in the local currency, where the library computes one.

inference.description: The estimate is the library's inference (Ghana penalty units at GHS 12), not a stated amount.

type.description:
The unit. money is in minor units of `currency`; duration is in seconds; hour is an hour of
the day in Africa/Lagos time; flag is 0 or 1.

default.description: Null when the institution must set the value.

value.description: The value in this environment (configured, else the default); null when unset.

max.description: For regulatory limits, the legal maximum.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, set only when the source states a full date.

action.description: What the system does (controls only), verbatim.

points.description: The library's points column (signals only), verbatim.

applies_to.description: Licence types the rule applies to. Empty means every institution.

requires.description: Capabilities the workspace must have for the rule to apply.

inputs.description: The data the rule needs. When one is unavailable the rule is reported as not evaluated.

events.description: The event types the rule is evaluated on.

applicable.description: Whether the rule applies to the workspace's profile; null without a profile.

config_version.description: The rule's configuration version in this environment; 0 means the library's defaults.

jurisdiction.description: The country of the pack the rule is in.

provenance.description:
Where the rule comes from (country libraries): a cited law (regulatory), a published typology
with no mandated number (industry_practice), or the library author's design, whose numbers are
starting values, not regulation (my_design).

off_reason.description: Why the rule ships switched off.

inherited_from.description: The pack an inherited rule comes from (`ng`); it keeps its ID and logic, with settings restated for the country.

template.description: The rule whose logic a parameterised rule reuses (ATO-01).

changes.description: The settings an inherited or parameterised rule changes from its parent.

basis.description: The library's "Tag, lineage, default, basis" column, verbatim.

engineering_logic.description: The library's section 7B logic. Only for `compliance:engineering`.

definition.description: The machine definition the engine interprets. Only for `compliance:engineering`.

currency.description: Amounts in this country's rules are in minor units of this currency.

minor_unit.description: Digits after the decimal point (2 for pesewas, 0 for Rwandan francs).

booking_entity.description: The licensed entity events name in `compliance.booking_entity`.

status.description: Shadow runs every rule in shadow; draft and suspended run none.

fallback.description: Judges events that name no booking entity (or one not activated).

events.description: The `compliance.kind` values that trigger the rule.

facts.description: The `compliance.facts` the rule reads (facts RiskOS computes are not listed).

refs.description: The `compliance.refs` its time windows are kept for.

unset_settings.description: Settings with no value yet; until they are set the rule is not evaluated.

kind.description: How the rule relates to the first library's rules ("Param of ATO-01", "New local").

current.description: The pack the workspace's fallback activation uses.

activated.description: The workspace has an activation in this jurisdiction.

since.description: Start of the first UTC day counted.

evaluations.description: Evaluations (not dry runs) in the period.

daily.description: Matches per UTC day, oldest first, one entry per day of the period.

truncated.description: More evaluations in the period than were checked (the newest 5,000 were).

amount.description: Minor units of currency, for transactions.

hours.description:
The deadline in hours; 0 means immediately. Null when the law sets a deadline no readable
source states (`kind` not_found): shown as "not found", never as zero.

authority.description: The body the clock runs against (FIC, BoG, NCSA), when the library names one.

ComplianceClockKind.description:
What a clock rests on: a deadline a law or regulator sets (legal), the institution's own
target (internal_policy), a design default standing in for a deadline not yet found
(design_placeholder), or a legal deadline no readable source states (not_found).

kind.description: Two sources disagree (conflict), or a fact was not found or not confirmed (unverified).

treatment.description: How the library handles it until a person settles it.

confirmed.description:
False for the profile every workspace gets automatically until a person saves it: its
licence type ("other") is a placeholder. Automatic profiles start the regulatory
controls at their defaults and every risk signal off.

missing.description: Answers still needed before submitting, by field name.

review_note.description: The reviewer's note (always given when rejected).

enabled.description: When false, the connection is kept but nobody can sign in with it.

redirect_uri.description: The callback to register at the identity provider.

client_secret.description: Required the first time; leave out to keep the stored secret.

mfa_methods.description: Second factors the user can complete sign-in with.

recovery_codes.description: Newly issued recovery codes, shown only in this response.

WebAuthnOptions.description: WebAuthn options, passed to the browser's credentials API as returned.

production_enabled.description: False for a self-serve workspace until RiskOS approves its onboarding; production requests get 403 `PRODUCTION_LOCKED` meanwhile.

environments.description: Choose one per request with the `RiskOS-Environment` header (default `test`).

reauth_valid_until.description: Until when high-impact actions are allowed without verifying again.

email_sent_at.description: When RiskOS emailed the link; absent or null if it has not.

invite_url.description: Single-use link, shown only in this response.

email_queued.description: True when the link is also being emailed to the invitee (RiskOS has email configured).

failing_since.description: When the current run of failed attempts started. After 3 days the endpoint is disabled.

previous_secret_valid_until.description: End of the current rotation overlap, if any.

secret.description: The signing secret. Shown only in this response; store it in a secrets manager.

overlap_hours.description: How long the previous secret keeps signing deliveries.

event_id.description: The event's ID (`RiskOS-Webhook-Id`), the same for every endpoint and every retry.

attempts.description: Attempts in the current delivery cycle (at most 9 over about an hour).

error.description: A short reason such as `timeout` or `http status 500`. Response bodies are never stored.

payload.description: The exact JSON body sent (signatures cover its bytes as sent).

AlertKind.description: `risk`: an evaluation reached the alert threshold. `security`: evaluations ran with missing signals.

subject.description: What the alert is about: the customer's user reference, or the environment for security alerts.

evaluation_count.description: Evaluations grouped into this alert (same subject, each within an hour of the previous).

actor.description: The API key or system job that acted.

assignee.description: Free-text reference to the analyst (for example an email or staff ID); empty to unassign.

message.description: Human-readable, safe-to-display description. Never contains internals.

checks.description: Status per dependency, keyed by dependency name.

Scope.description:
A permission. API keys can hold any except `rules:approve`, `compliance:write`,
`compliance:configure` and `compliance:sensitive`, which only people hold (a second person
approves production rule changes; a person sets the compliance profile and configures pack
rules; only compliance officers see suspicious transaction reports and compliance-only
signals).

prefix.description: The non-secret start of the key, for recognizing it (e.g. in logs of the caller's own systems).

replaced_by.description: The key that replaced this one through rotation.

secret.description: The full API key. Shown only in this response and never retrievable again.

expires_at.description: Optional expiry; must be in the future.

overlap_seconds.description: How long the old key keeps working after rotation (default 24 hours, maximum 7 days).

sequence.description: Position in the tenant's hash chain (1-based, gap-free across all environments).

type.description:
`staff` is RiskOS staff reading this tenant with support access that the tenant's
log also shows being requested and approved by two different staff members.

hash.description: Hex SHA-256 of this entry chained to prev_hash.

Event.description:
An event, discriminated by `type`. Each type has its own `data` shape; unknown fields are
rejected everywhere. Identifiers are the customer's own opaque references: do not send
names, emails or other personal data as identifiers.

ActivityEvent.description:
Account or platform activity that is neither a money movement nor a sign-in (an account
opened, an API request, a data export, a staff action...). `compliance.kind` says which.

ComplianceContext.description:
What the workspace's rule pack needs about the event (ADR-0006; EVENTS.md#compliance).
Everything is optional: a rule whose data is missing is reported as not evaluated, never
treated as no risk.

facts.description:
Facts from your systems and providers, by the names in the pack's catalog
(`device.rooted`, `telco.sim_swap`, `customer.type`...): true or false, a number (a
duration in seconds, a count, a ratio, a score), one of the fact's listed values, or
for amounts `{"amount": <minor units>, "currency": "NGN"}`. Facts RiskOS computes
itself (behaviour history, workflows, the amount and identifiers of the event) are
refused.

booking_entity.description:
The licensed entity that holds the customer relationship, as activated in the workspace
(ADR-0007). Its jurisdiction's pack judges the event; without it, the workspace's fallback
activation does, and with no fallback the event is reported as jurisdiction unresolved.

data_subject_country.description: The country of the person whose data the event concerns, for data-protection rules only.

ComplianceRefs.description:
Opaque references for the entities rules keep time windows for. Never the BVN, phone
number, card number or address itself: send your own reference for it.

ComplianceEventKind.description:
What the event is, in the rule pack's terms. Money kinds go with `transaction` events,
sign-in kinds with `login`, `device_bound` and `device_reregistered` with `device_change`,
and the others with `activity`. Without it, RiskOS derives the kind from the event (a debit
is `transfer_outbound`, a credit `transfer_inbound`, a failed login `auth_failure`...).

SessionChangeEvent.description: A session was created, refreshed or ended.

EventKey.description: The customer's unique ID for the event; the idempotency key.

ip.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address of the end user.

GeoPoint.description:
Where the end user was, for impossible-travel checks (BEH-02). RiskOS rounds it to 2
decimals (about 1 km) before storing it.

amount.description: Amount in minor units of the currency (e.g. cents).

RiskLevel.description:
The risk band of a score: minimal, low, elevated, high, critical (default thresholds
20/50/70/90, adjustable per environment; see `GET /api/v1/risk/policy`).

RiskThresholds.description: Lowest score of each band above minimal; must increase strictly. Always present in responses; when omitted from a PUT, the defaults are stored.

custom_calibration.description: True when the environment's thresholds differ from the defaults.

AutoBlockMode.description:
`off`: Critical scores get REVIEW. `shadow`: they still get REVIEW, and the evaluation is
marked `would_block` in its policy reasons, to gather evidence. `on`: they get BLOCK
(possible only after 14 days in shadow). Switching to `off` or `shadow` takes effect at
once: it is the kill switch.

shadow_since.description: When shadow evidence started (kept while blocking is on). Set by the server; ignored in a PUT.

shadow_days_required.description: Days in shadow mode before blocking can be switched on.

eligible_at.description: From when blocking can be switched on (null when not in shadow or on).

would_block_last_14_days.description: Evaluations in the last 14 days that blocking would have blocked.

RiskDecision.description:
The risk response (spec §7). risk_score is the sum of the listed signal weights, capped at
100. degraded_signals lists sources that could not be evaluated for this event.
warming_signals lists history signals held back while behavioural history rebuilds after
RiskOS lost it (see docs/DISASTER_RECOVERY.md); it is empty otherwise.

request_id.description: The request that produced this decision (for replays, the original request).

event_id.description: RiskOS ID of the stored event; null for dry runs.

controls.description:
The regulatory controls of the workspace's rule pack that applied to the event (see the
console's Rules library). A live control's decision is reflected in `decision`; a shadow
control is reported only. Empty without a compliance profile.

not_evaluated.description:
Rules of the pack the event triggered that could not be evaluated because data or a
setting they need was unavailable. Missing data is never treated as no risk: send the
listed facts in the event's `compliance` block, or set the listed settings.

JurisdictionResolution.description:
Which country's pack judged the event and why (ADR-0007): the booking entity the event named,
the workspace's stated fallback, or none (`unresolved`: no pack judged it; `inactive`: the
booking entity's activation is in draft or suspended). Absent for workspaces with no activation.

jurisdiction.description: The governing country; absent when unresolved or inactive.

pack.description: The pack version that judged the event (gh@2026.10.1).

tasks.description: What the institution must do (report.CTR, case.open, edd...).

hold_seconds.description: The longest the funds may be held.

exemption_unknown.description: The control applied because its exemption could not be checked.

missing.description:
What was unavailable: `fact:<name>` (send it in `compliance.facts`), `setting:<name>`
(set it for the rule), `history:<window>` (behaviour history, or a reference the window
is kept for) or `currency:<fact>` (an amount in another currency than the rule's).

TransactionSummary.description: For transactions, the fields an analyst scans for.

event_count.description: Events in the profile (at most the most recent 5,000).

flagged.description: Events that got Review or Block.

normalized_payload.description: The canonical form the risk engine evaluated.

RuleCondition.description:
A condition tree. Each node is exactly one of:
`{"all": [node, ...]}`, `{"any": [node, ...]}`, `{"not": node}`, or a comparison
`{"field": "<field>", "op": "<operator>", "value": <value>}`. Fields and their operators
are listed by `GET /api/v1/risk/catalog`. At most 50 nodes, 6 levels deep, 100 list
items. A comparison on a field the event does not have never matches.

RuleMode.description: active rules add their weight to the score; shadow rules are only recorded.

code.description: Signal code the rule emits when it matches.

restored_from.description: Set when this version restored an earlier one.

updated_at.description: When the current version was created.

pending_change_id.description: A proposed change awaiting approval (production), if any.

total.description: Entries in the environment, including those not listed here.

limit.description: The most entries an environment can have.

rule_id.description: The rule changed, or for a new rule the ID it gets when approved.

base_version.description: The rule's version when proposed (null for a new rule).

reason.description: Why it was rejected, when given.

version.description: The version tested; null when a draft condition was tested.

facts.description: Values of the fields the condition references, for this event.

weights.description: Overrides of built-in signal weights (0-50), keyed by signal code.

high_value_default.description:
High-value threshold in minor units for currencies without their own entry. While any
signal source is degraded, events at or above it get at least REVIEW.

fail_policies.description:
What a degraded evaluation falls back to, per event type: `closed` (at least REVIEW)
or `open` (allow, flagged). Types not listed fail closed.

alert_min_decision.description:
The least severe decision that raises an alert. Always present in responses; when
omitted from a PUT, `review` is stored.

auto_block.description:
Automatic blocking of Critical scores. Always present in responses; when omitted from
a PUT, the current mode is kept. Switching it on requires 14 days in shadow mode.

weight.description: Effective weight in the caller's environment.

strengthenable.description: Whether the signal turns a Low-band score into STEP_UP.

label.description: What the fact is, in plain words.

group.description: Event, Transaction, Login, Customer history or Recent activity.

unit.description:
How a number reads: money (minor units of the event's currency), count, or ratio
(1.5 = one and a half times).

kind.description: A free-text string that is an ISO country or currency code.

values.description: The only values a string field takes, with their labels.

events.description: The event types that carry the fact; empty means every event.
